clue.text: Compelled company to have new creed

indicators.note: new tells us the word creed is made afresh, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm is forced to adopt a fresh statement of belief.
explanation.definitionFit: To be compelled is to be forced, which is exactly what coerced means.

clue.text: Rises for many members

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, used for many
limbs such as arms and legs are members of the body

explanation.surface: A club's ranks go up thanks to a large membership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'many' stands for C, a hundred in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to go upward, the same as ascending a slope or ladder.

clue.text: Terse arrangement about a holiday that's not fixed

indicators.note: about places the shuffled letters around a
arrangement says the word terse has its letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A curt note concerning a festival whose date moves each year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns TERSE into ESTER, and 'about' puts that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: This Christian festival is a moveable feast, its date set by the moon.

clue.text: What made chicken opt for a secure road crossing

indicators.note: made signals the letters of chicken opt are formed into something new

explanation.surface: The old joke asks why the chicken crossed the road, here at a guarded post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' and 'for a' are link words; the surface plays on the joke about the chicken crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded barrier where traffic or people are stopped and inspected.

clue.text: Overshadow friend of Snow White

definitions.meaning: to make something look small by comparison
one of the seven small companions in the fairy tale

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to dwarf by comparison and names one of the seven little men of the fairy tale.

clue.text: Quits at university levels

parts.note: being quits means being square, or evens, with someone
a student who is up is in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student drops out while at college, seeking a level footing.
explanation.definitionFit: To level a contest is to make it equal, the phrasal verb meaning to equalise.

clue.text: Try an overdue reform

indicators.note: reform means to form again, so an overdue is rearranged

explanation.surface: Attempt a reform that should have come long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Try and this word are synonyms for an attempt or effort.

clue.text: American water goes up in S Ireland

indicators.note: goes up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes in North America

explanation.surface: Water from America flows upward in the south of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish name for the state occupying the south of the island.

clue.text: Pupils start to sing newly composed chorals

indicators.note: start to picks out the opening letter of sing
newly composed says the letters of chorals are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Children begin singing freshly written choral pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are learners, and this word also means people being taught.

clue.text: Pastor to cook Sunday lunch perhaps?

indicators.note: to cook figuratively is to falsify, so pastor to is reworked

explanation.surface: The vicar has to prepare the Sunday dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowly cooked joint of beef is a typical British Sunday meal, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Could be a periodical dispute

definitions.meaning: a single numbered edition of a magazine or journal
a point in contention, as in taking a matter up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one edition of a magazine and a matter under debate.

clue.text: Hold rates for building in garrison town

indicators.note: building suggests construction, so the letters of hold rates are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing the rents charged on construction in an army town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; this Hampshire town is the traditional home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hampshire town has been the base of the British Army since the 1850s, a classic garrison settlement.

clue.text: It dawns on most people while they're in bed

definitions.text: It dawns on most people while they're in bed

parts.words: It dawns on most people while they're in bed
parts.note: the phrase is taken literally: daybreak arrives while people sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the moment dawn arrives, usually before most people wake.

clue.text: Too wrapped up in financial solvency

indicators.note: wrapped up in signals the answer is concealed within the run of words financial solvency

explanation.surface: Someone is equally absorbed in keeping their money matters healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and the answer are synonyms meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Tight struggle to end with marriage

parts.note: to close is to end or finish
a match is a marriage or a good pairing

explanation.surface: A tough fight that finishes with a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest whose outcome is narrowly decided is a tight struggle.

clue.text: Where members are entitled to sit

definitions.text: Where members are entitled to sit

parts.words: Where members are entitled to sit
parts.note: entitled is read as having titles: peers sit in the upper chamber of Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: The upper chamber of the UK Parliament, whose members are mainly titled peers.

clue.text: Thrown into a suit case

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters of into a suit are tossed about

explanation.surface: Someone is bundled into a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A case can mean a set of circumstances, as in in that case.

clue.text: Look at lads running amok — they're shocking

parts.note: to scan is to look at closely

indicators.note: running amok suggests the letters of lads go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Observe boys out of control, a shocking sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrages that cause public shock are disgraceful affairs.

clue.text: A run caused by panic in the stock market?

definitions.text: A run caused by panic in the stock market?

parts.words: A run caused by panic in the stock market?
parts.note: stock is livestock, not shares: a herd bolting in panic

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a herd of cattle or horses.

clue.text: Score with awkward truths in clever argument

parts.note: to score is to cut a line into a surface
with and and both mean together with

indicators.note: awkward suggests the word truths is clumsily arranged, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A debater wins a point by voicing uncomfortable facts in a sharp exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes lively, skilful debate, borrowed from swordplay.

clue.text: A sticker for the traditional method of roasting

definitions.text: A sticker for the traditional method of roasting

parts.words: A sticker for the traditional method of roasting
parts.note: a sticker here is something that sticks or pierces meat, and also a stickler for tradition

explanation.definitionFit: A long pin used to hold meat for roasting over a fire.

clue.text: They were banned from moving debris

indicators.note: moving says the letters of debris are shifted about

explanation.surface: Moving rubble was prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned' puns on banns, the public notices read in church before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Women about to marry have their banns read, so they were banned in a punning sense.

clue.text: Cite a famous person

definitions.meaning: to mention or specify someone or something

explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean to mention specifically, and also a well-known figure.

clue.text: Horologist to keep eye on manufacturer

parts.note: to keep an eye on something is to watch it
a manufacturer is a maker of goods

explanation.surface: A clockmaker needs to keep an eye on the firm that makes the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A horologist studies or makes timepieces, so this craftsman is one.

clue.text: Price of a suit?

parts.note: suit is a lawsuit, not clothing: legal fees awarded

explanation.definitionFit: Legal expenses of a lawsuit, which a court may order the loser to pay.

clue.text: An inclination to show prejudice

definitions.meaning: a leaning or tendency, as in a slant

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a leaning or slant and unfair partiality.

clue.text: Drinks for parties, if stirred

indicators.note: stirred, as of a cocktail, signals the letters of parties and if are mixed

explanation.surface: Cocktails for gatherings, provided they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are alcoholic drinks taken before a meal to whet the appetite.

clue.text: Drawn towards marriage!

parts.note: to means towards, as in walking to the shop
wed is to marry, here standing for the marriage

explanation.surface: Someone feels attracted to the idea of getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn means pulled along behind, as a trailer is hauled by a car.

clue.text: Tramples relative?

definitions.meaning: treads heavily on, as two words
a family member: a spouse's son by an earlier partner

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means treads on; as one, a partner's son from a previous relationship.

clue.text: They look round, quietly present on board

indicators.note: on, read as aboard, places the following pieces within the vessel

parts.note: board stands for a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship quietly look about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look round' is not glancing about: the definition means they appear round in shape. 'on board' puts P and HERE inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Globes and orbs appear round in shape, which is what these solids are.
